---
title: "About this dashboard"
---

## What this is

The **West Boundary Water Security** dashboard is a pilot tool developed to
support the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary (RDKB) and the KRWAC
Agriculture and Water Working Group in planning for agricultural water supply and
storage in the West Boundary (Kettle River watershed, Midway and upstream).

Its purpose is to make public water information easy to see and understand, so
that producers, First Nations, local government, provincial agencies, and other
water users can share a common picture of seasonal conditions and drought risk.

## Planning and engagement only

This dashboard is for **planning and community engagement purposes only**. It is
**not** a regulatory or compliance monitoring tool. Live readings are provisional
and unverified and should not be used for enforcement or for decisions that
require official, quality-assured data.

## Data sources

- **Streamflow** — Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) real-time
  hydrometric service and the Water Survey of Canada HYDAT historical database,
  accessed with the open-source `tidyhydat` R package.
- **Groundwater** — B.C. Provincial Groundwater Observation Well Network (PGOWN).
- All data are public and provided under open licences (including the Open
  Government Licence – British Columbia).

## Privacy and responsible use

The dashboard uses **public and voluntarily shared information only**. If
producer-contributed inputs are added in future (for example well levels, repeat
photo points, or irrigation timing), they would be **aggregated or anonymised** so
that individual operations cannot be identified, consistent with FOIPPA and with
the project's commitment to a transparent, non-regulatory process.

## Ownership and upkeep

The dashboard is built entirely with open-source tools (Quarto + R) so it can be
fully owned, hosted, and maintained by the Regional District. Source files,
data-build scripts, and documentation are included in the project repository, and
the historical baselines can be refreshed with a single command.
